title: Extending connective coverage: 9 verified additions, 9 candidates measured and dropped
goal: A bounded next step on EXP-090's own conclusion: extend CONNECTIVE_TABLE/DISCOURSE_ADVERBIAL_TABLE coverage past ~20/149 DiMLex-Eng connectives, verifying each candidate against real spaCy output before adding it -- and reporting, not hiding, any candidate that doesn't fit this module's existing structural patterns.
method: 18 candidate connectives, spanning all four PDTB classes, probed directly against spaCy's real dependency parse before any table entry was written. 9 cleanly matched one of the two existing structural patterns (mark+advcl for while/whereas; sentence-initial advmod+ROOT for the 7 discourse adverbials) and were added to CONNECTIVE_TABLE/DISCOURSE_ADVERBIAL_TABLE. 9 did not and were left out. One hand-built sentence per added connective, plus a sweep of the real GDPR_TEXT fixture for instances of the new connectives specifically. Reran EXP-090/091/026/050 to confirm the additions caused no regression.
results_prose: 9/9 new connectives correctly classified -- all correct, covering 2 more mark+advcl subordinators (while, whereas) and 7 more sentence-initial discourse adverbials (meanwhile, subsequently, accordingly, additionally, similarly, likewise, conversely), all verified against real spaCy output before being added, the same discipline EXP-090 used. 9 further candidates were measured and deliberately dropped rather than forced into a wrong classification -- each hits a genuinely different structural pattern this module doesn't yet handle (ccomp complementizers, compound prepositions, stacked advmods), named honestly in follow_ups. On the real GDPR text: 0 instances of the 9 new connectives found.
conclusion: Connective coverage grew from 28 to 37 recognized phrases (CONNECTIVE_TABLE + DISCOURSE_ADVERBIAL_TABLE combined) through the same two already-built, already-tested structural patterns -- no new detection code, purely additive table entries. Equally important: 9 further candidates were measured and found NOT to fit either existing pattern, and were left out rather than misclassified -- extending coverage further needs new structural patterns (a ccomp-vs-mark discriminator for 'that'-clauses, multi-token compound prepositions), not just more table rows.
scale_down: Still a small, named subset of DiMLex-Eng's 149 (37 now, not all 149). The 9 dropped candidates are real, nameable future work (see follow_ups), not abandoned without reason. Hand-built sentences, not held-out novel phrasings of the same connectives.
follow_ups: assuming that: 'that' attaches via dep_=='ccomp', the excluded reported-speech-complementizer pattern (EXP-090)
now that: 'that' attaches via dep_=='ccomp', same as 'assuming that'
given that: 'given' attaches as dep_=='prep' to an ACOMP, not the ROOT verb -- different shape than existing prep-subordinator entries
whenever: surfaces as dep_=='advmod' (not 'mark') attached to an advcl -- a new pattern this module doesn't check
as soon as: two stacked advmod tokens attached directly to ROOT, not mark+advcl at all
due to: two-token 'X to' compound preposition; the object sits under the second token, not the first the way _clause_text_for_prep expects
owing to: same two-token compound-preposition shape as 'due to'
in spite of: three-token idiom ('in spite OF'); only partially fits the existing two-token _IN_IDIOMS extension point
regardless of: three-token idiom with its own 'regardless' as advmod, not prep -- a different shape from 'in spite of'
models_used: spaCy en_core_web_sm dependency parser via lab.common.connectives.find_connectives (unchanged detection code, new table entries only). No generative model.
